questions.question: Evaluate 23³ + (-15)³ + (-8)³
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the sum of three numbers **a + b + c = 0**, then the identity **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc** holds true.

Here, **a = 23**, **b = −15**, and **c = −8**.

Sum: **23 + (−15) + (−8) = 23 − 23 = 0**.

Result: **3 × 23 × (−15) × (−8) = 69 × 120 = 8280**.

**∴ The correct answer is 8280.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: **23³ + (−15)³ + (−8)³**

**Formula Used:**

**a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8cbf19edb5d31e8ceb91486a99d4db415bf7e4518ccf0e8df66c7f4c51d34489.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **a = 23**, **b = −15**, **c = −8**

⇒ First, check the sum: **a + b + c = 23 + (−15) + (−8) = 0**

⇒ Substitute **(a + b + c) = 0** into the identity:

⇒ **a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (0) × (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)**

⇒ **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc**

⇒ **Value = 3 × 23 × (−15) × (−8)**

⇒ **Value = 3 × 23 × 120 = 69 × 120 = 8280**

**∴ The correct answer is 8280.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identity of Cubes

The general form is **a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)**. This is a fundamental identity used to simplify cubic expressions.

Zero Sum Condition

When the variables satisfy **a + b + c = 0**, the entire right-hand side of the identity becomes zero, leading directly to the relation **a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc**.

Square of a Trinomial

Another related identity is **(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)**, which is often used in conjunction with the cubic identity in competitive exams.

questions.question: Two trains of lengths 120 m and 180 m are moving in the same direction at speeds of 60 km/h and 40 km/h, respectively. Find the time taken by the trains to cross each other.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total length** to be covered = 120 + 180 = 300 m

**Relative speed** (same direction) = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h

Convert speed to m/s ⇒ 20 × 5/18 = 50/9 m/s

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 300 ÷ (50/9) = 54 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 54 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 120 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 180 m

Speed of first train (v₁) = 60 km/h

Speed of second train (v₂) = 40 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a98cb8917ad4bd84df1b98cbd2d635f74d5254f0e82cfb34040aa9f2fff7aaea.png] 

When two objects move in the **same direction**, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds.

⇒ Total Distance (D) = L₁ + L₂

⇒ D = 120 + 180 = 300 m

⇒ Relative Speed (Vᵣₑₗ) = v₁ − v₂

⇒ Vᵣₑₗ = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by 5/18:

⇒ Vᵣₑₗ = 20 × (5/18) = 100/18 = 50/9 m/s

**Time taken (T)** = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ T = 300 ÷ (50/9)

⇒ T = (300 × 9) ÷ 50

⇒ T = 6 × 9 = 54 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 54 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two trains move toward each other, the relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Vᵣₑₗ = v₁ + v₂.

Unit Conversion Rule

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing a Stationary Point Object

When a train crosses a pole or a standing man, the distance covered is equal to the length of the train itself.

questions.question: Find the value of (3+(4)/(3) of 2(1)/(4)div 2(2)/(5)-2(1)/(4) of 3(1)/(5))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expression: (3 + 4/3 of 2(1/4) ÷ 2(2/5) − 2(1/4) of 3(1/5))

**Formula used:**

Follow the **BODMAS rule** (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

**Calculation:**

First, convert the **mixed fractions** into **improper fractions**:

⇒ 2(1/4) = 9/4

⇒ 2(2/5) = 12/5

⇒ 3(1/5) = 16/5

Substitute these values into the expression:

⇒ 3 + 4/3 of 9/4 ÷ 12/5 − 9/4 of 16/5

Solve the **'of'** operations:

⇒ 4/3 of 9/4 = 4/3 × 9/4 = 3

⇒ 9/4 of 16/5 = 9/4 × 16/5 = 36/5 = 7.2

The expression now becomes:

⇒ 3 + 3 ÷ 12/5 − 7.2

Next, solve the **division**:

⇒ 3 ÷ 12/5 = 3 × 5/12 = 1.25

Now, perform the **addition** and **subtraction**:

⇒ 3 + 1.25 − 7.2

⇒ 4.25 − 7.2

⇒ −2.95

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: 10 men and 15 women can complete a project in 12 days. If after 8 days, only 2/3 of the work is completed, how many more women must be added to finish the work in the next 2 days, assuming all men continue?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the daily work of 10 men and 15 women together be represented as 1 combined unit.

Total work done in 8 days = 8 units, which is 2/3 of the work. Remaining work = 1/3 of the work = 4 units.

To complete 4 units of work in 2 days, the daily requirement = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 units of work per day.

Since 10 men and 15 women provide 1 unit of work per day, we need 2 times the initial workforce to get 2 units per day.

Required workforce = 2 × (10 men + 15 women) = 20 men + 30 women. Since only men continue (10 men) and we need to find extra women, we can double the women component to reach the required work rate: 15 more women are already equivalent to the extra 10 men's share.

Let's use the standard formula: (10M + 15W) × 8 / (2/3) = (10M + 15W + xW) × 2 / (1/3)

⇒ (10M + 15W) × 4 = (10M + 15W + xW) × 2

⇒ 20M + 30W = 10M + 15W + xW

⇒ xW = 10M + 15W.

Since 10M + 15W can do 1/12 of the work per day, and 2/3 of work in 8 days matches perfectly, the addition of 10M + 15W worth of efficiency is required.

Since 10M + 15W = 25W equivalent (from work rate), the extra women needed is 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 women.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Initial group: 10 men and 15 women can complete the project in 12 days.

⇒ Work completed in 8 days = 2/3 of the total work.

⇒ Remaining work = 1 − 2/3 = 1/3 of the total work.

⇒ Time available to finish the remaining work = 2 days.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ (M₁ × D₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂) / W₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the daily work capacity of 10 men and 15 women combined be E₁.

⇒ E₁ × 12 = Total Work (W)

⇒ In 8 days, work done = E₁ × 8 = 8/12 of W = 2/3 of W. This matches the given condition.

⇒ To complete the remaining 1/3 of W in 2 days, the required daily efficiency E₂ must satisfy:

⇒ E₂ × 2 = 1/3 × (E₁ × 12)

⇒ E₂ × 2 = 4 × E₁

⇒ E₂ = 2 × E₁

⇒ This means the new workforce must have twice the efficiency of the initial workforce.

⇒ New Workforce = 2 × (10 Men + 15 Women) = 20 Men + 30 Women

⇒ Since only 10 Men continue, the remaining capacity must be fulfilled by women.

⇒ Efficiency of 10 Men + 15 Women + x Women = 20 Men + 30 Women

⇒ 15 Women + x Women = 10 Men + 30 Women

⇒ x Women = 10 Men + 15 Women

⇒ Since 10 men and 15 women can complete 1/12 of the work daily, and from the relation of work rates we know that 10 men and 15 women can be replaced entirely by 25 women to maintain the same rate of completion under the standard efficiency ratio:

⇒ x = 25

**∴ The correct answer is 25 women.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Work Equivalence Formula

The relationship between men, women, days, and work can be generalized as (m × M + w × W) × D / Work = Constant, where M and W represent the efficiency of one man and one woman respectively.

Pipes & Cisterns Analogy

Similar to people working, pipes filling a tank use the same efficiency addition concept where Total Capacity = Sum of individual rates × Time taken.

questions.question: A cylindrical water tank has a radius of 7 cm and a height of 10 cm. What is its volume? (Use π = 22/7)

For a circle with **radius 7 cm**, the **base area** is a standard value: 154 cm².

**Volume of Cylinder** = **Base Area** × **Height**

⇒ Volume = 154 × 10 = 1540 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 1540 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Radius (r)** of the tank = 7 cm

**Height (h)** of the tank = 10 cm

Value of **π** = 22/7

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8db534567b41501a812638dba0464a2cd86331fd008de0f22edd95bdc7f14ae0.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Volume (V)** of a cylinder = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = (22/7) × 7 × 7 × 10

⇒ Volume = 22 × 7 × 10

⇒ Volume = 154 × 10

⇒ Volume = 1540 cm³

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the side surface of the cylinder is given by the formula 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of the area of the curved surface and the two circular bases is 2πr(r + h).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same **radius** and **height** as a cylinder has exactly (1/3) of its volume: V = (1/3)πr²h.

questions.question: A prize of ₹8,400 is to be shared between A and B in the ratio 3:5. Find B’s share.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total ratio parts of **A** and **B** = 3 + 5 = 8 units.

8 units → ₹8,400

1 unit → 8400 ÷ 8 = ₹1,050

**B**'s share (5 units) = 5 × 1,050 = ₹5,250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount to be shared = **₹8,400**

Ratio of **A** : **B** = **3 : 5**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/01f2ba984afa2f77193cd3975a4e79f2b4fc0d8b2d07c1eeaac01055a2e099bd.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Share of a person = (Personal Ratio Part ÷ Sum of Ratio Parts) × Total Amount

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 3 + 5 = 8

⇒ **B**'s share = (5 ÷ 8) × 8,400

⇒ **B**'s share = 5 × (8,400 ÷ 8)

⇒ **B**'s share = 5 × 1,050

⇒ **B**'s share = ₹5,250

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5,250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Distribution

If a quantity Q is divided in the ratio a:b, then the first part is [a/(a+b)] × Q and the second part is [b/(a+b)] × Q.

Inverse Ratio

The inverse ratio of a:b is 1/a : 1/b, which simplifies to b:a.

Compound Ratio

For two ratios a:b and c:d, the compound ratio is (a × c) : (b × d).

questions.question: Two poles of heights 10 m and 30 m stand vertically on level ground at a distance d apart. From a point on the ground between them, along the line joining their feet, the angles of elevation to their tops of the taller and the shorter poles are 60∘ and 30∘, respectively. The distance d between the poles is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Base distance from **shorter pole** (10 m) for 30° = 10 × √3 = 10√3 m.

Base distance from **taller pole** (30 m) for 60° = 30 / √3 = 10√3 m.

Total distance **d** = 10√3 + 10√3 = 20√3 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Height** of shorter pole (H₁) = 10 m, **Height** of taller pole (H₂) = 30 m, **Angles of elevation** = 30° and 60°.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/81683b23de5306f914bc4f62694cbfa86b7d4bdb46a8408e992d43c27c7dc586.png] 

Let the distance from the **shorter pole** to point P be **x** and from the **taller pole** to point P be **y**.

For the **shorter pole** (Height = 10 m, θ = 30°):

⇒ tan 30° = 10 / x

⇒ 1 / √3 = 10 / x

⇒ x = 10√3 m

For the **taller pole** (Height = 30 m, θ = 60°):

⇒ tan 60° = 30 / y

⇒ √3 = 30 / y

⇒ y = 30 / √3 = (30 × √3) / 3 = 10√3 m

Total **distance** between the poles **d**:

⇒ d = x + y

⇒ d = 10√3 + 10√3

⇒ d = 20√3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 20√3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Elevation

The angle formed by the line of sight with the horizontal when an object is viewed above the horizontal level.

Trigonometric Ratios for Heights

Common values used: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Pythagoras Theorem

In right-angled triangles, Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 12 days, respectively. Both work for 3 days and then A leaves. How long (in days) will B take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Work** (LCM of 12, 12) = 12 units; Efficiency of **A** = 1, **B** = 1.

Combined efficiency of (**A** + **B**) = 1 + 1 = 2 units/day.

Work done in **3 days** = 2 × 3 = 6 units.

**Remaining work** = 12 − 6 = 6 units.

Time for **B** to finish = 6 units ÷ 1 unit/day = 6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Combined efficiency of **A** and **B** = 1 + 1 = 2 units per day.

⇒ Work completed by **A** and **B** in **3 days** = 2 × 3 = 6 units.

⇒ **Remaining work** = Total work − Completed work = 12 − 6 = 6 units.

⇒ Time taken by **B** to complete the **remaining work** = 6 ÷ 1 = 6 days.

Efficiency and Time Relation

questions.question: What is the compound interest on ₹3,000 for 2 years at 20% per annum, interest compounded annually?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate for 2 years at 20% p.a. = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20) ÷ 100 = 44%.

Compound Interest = 44% of ₹3,000.

CI = 3,000 × 0.44 = ₹1,320.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,320.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ and CI = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50e9d042a9cecf43668d09957230c7479a47b6230c9729a3ac291bbe2cc5156c.png] 

⇒ A = 3,000 × (1 + 20 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 3,000 × (120 ÷ 100) × (120 ÷ 100)

⇒ A = 3,000 × 1.2 × 1.2

⇒ A = 3,000 × 1.44

⇒ A = ₹4,320

⇒ CI = 4,320 − 3,000

⇒ CI = ₹1,320

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,320.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI and SI Difference (for 2 years)

For successive growth of x% and y%, the total growth is x + y + (xy ÷ 100)%. For 2 years at rate R, it is 2R + (R² ÷ 100)%.

Compounding Frequencies

questions.question: If 2, x, and 18 are in continued proportion, find the positive value of x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When numbers **a, b, and c** are in **continued proportion**, **b** is the **mean proportional**.

Logic: **b = √(a × c)**

Applying the trick: **x = √(2 × 18) = √36 = 6**

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers **2, x, and 18** are in **continued proportion**.

**Formula Used:**

Three numbers **a, b, and c** are said to be in **continued proportion** if **a/b = b/c**, which implies **b² = ac**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eabf4fa78b5c1ba122aaec1c13725e7107b77f63bb702faa03ccccbe60040b7f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 ÷ x = x ÷ 18

⇒ x² = 2 × 18

⇒ x² = 36

⇒ x = √36

⇒ x = 6 (as we need the positive value)

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The **mean proportional** between two numbers **a** and **b** is √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If **a, b, c** are in **continued proportion**, then **c** is called the **third proportional** to **a** and **b**, where **c = b²/a**.

Fourth Proportional

If **a:b = c:d**, then **d** is called the **fourth proportional** to **a, b, and c**, calculated as **d = (b × c) / a**.

questions.question: A spherical tank has a radius of 2 meters. If the tank is filled with water to 80% of its total volume, what is the volume of water in the tank (rounded to the nearest cubic meter)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total volume of **spherical tank** = (4/3) × π × r³.

Given r = 2 m, Total Volume = (4/3) × 3.14159 × 8 ≈ 33.51 m³.

**Water volume** = 80% of 33.51 = 0.8 × 33.51 ≈ 26.81 m³.

Rounding to the **nearest cubic meter**, we get 27 m³.

questions.question: During a sale, 50% of the goods are sold at 12% profit, 40% of the remaining goods are sold at 16% profit and the still remaining goods are sold at a loss of 19%. If there is an overall profit of x%, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of goods: **50%** (Part 1) : **20%** (40% of 50%, Part 2) : **30%** (Rest, Part 3).

Simplified ratio = **5 : 2 : 3**.

Apply **weighted average** for profit/loss: x = [(5 × 12) + (2 × 16) + (3 × −19)] ÷ (5 + 2 + 3).

x = [60 + 32 − 57] ÷ 10 = 35 ÷ 10 = **3.5**.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total goods = 100 units (Assumed CP = ₹100)

Part 1: **50%** of 100 = 50 units at **12% profit**

Remaining: 100 − 50 = 50 units

Part 2: **40% of remaining** = 0.40 × 50 = 20 units at **16% profit**

Part 3: **Still remaining** = 50 − 20 = 30 units at **19% loss**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a50de7c600b73029c08a3eee0d9fe33c3d2901c348c2f68aea5ce0a54db8baad.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit from Part 1 = 50 × 12 ÷ 100 = **6**

⇒ Profit from Part 2 = 20 × 16 ÷ 100 = **3.2**

⇒ Loss from Part 3 = 30 × 19 ÷ 100 = **5.7**

⇒ **Total Net Profit** = 6 + 3.2 − 5.7 = **3.5**

⇒ **Overall Profit Percentage (x)** = (Total Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ x = (3.5 ÷ 100) × 100 = **3.5**

**∴ The correct answer is 3.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question: A sum of money becomes ₹7,865 after 2 years and ₹8,651.50 after 3 years on compound interest at the same rate, compounded annually. Find the sum.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of interest = [(Difference in Amounts) ÷ (Amount after 2 years)] × 100

Rate (R) = [(8,651.50 − 7,865) ÷ 7,865] × 100 = (786.5 ÷ 7,865) × 100 = 10%

For R = 10%, Multiplying Factor for 2 years = (1.1)² = 1.21

Sum (P) = 7,865 ÷ 1.21 = ₹6,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Amount** after 2 years (A₂) = ₹7,865

**Amount** after 3 years (A₃) = ₹8,651.50

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

The interest for the 3rd year is the **compound interest** earned on the amount at the end of the 2ⁿd year.

⇒ Interest = A₃ − A₂

⇒ Interest = 8,651.50 − 7,865 = ₹786.50

⇒ Rate (R) = (786.50 ÷ 7,865) × 100 = 10%

Now, using the formula for 2 years:

⇒ 7,865 = P(1 + 10/100)²

⇒ 7,865 = P(1.1)²

⇒ 7,865 = P × 1.21

⇒ P = 7,865 ÷ 1.21

⇒ P = 6,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

SI vs CI for 2 Years

The difference between **Simple Interest** and **Compound Interest** for 2 years is given by D = P(R/100)².

questions.question: If one angle of an isosceles triangle is 110°, what are the measures of the other angles of the triangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an **isosceles triangle**, the angles opposite to equal sides are equal. Since **110°** is an obtuse angle, it cannot be repeated (as 110° + 110° > 180°).

Remaining sum for two equal angles = 180° − 110° = 70°

Individual base angles = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°

**∴ The correct answer is 35degree and 35degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

One angle of an **isosceles triangle** = 110°

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all internal angles of a triangle = 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/18e29b6938625314643e6a3121151d56101a43e8e46b70464c077bc212824bab.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the equal angles of the **isosceles triangle** be x.

In any triangle, sum of angles = 180°

⇒ 110° + x + x = 180°

⇒ 110° + 2x = 180°

⇒ 2x = 180° − 110°

⇒ 2x = 70°

⇒ x = 70° ÷ 2

⇒ x = 35°

**∴ The correct answer is 35degree and 35degree.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The sum of the three interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.

Isosceles Triangle Property

In an isosceles triangle, the angles opposite to the equal sides are equal in measure.

Obtuse Isosceles Triangle

A triangle can have only one obtuse angle (greater than 90°). In an isosceles triangle, the obtuse angle must be the vertex angle.

questions.question: The sum of the digits of a two-digit number is 11. If the digits are reversed, the new number is 27 more than the original number. What is the original number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between a **two-digit number** and its **reversed** version is always 9 × (difference of its digits).

Difference of digits = 27 ÷ 9 = 3.

Sum of digits is given as 11.

Digits are (11 + 3) ÷ 2 = 7 and (11 − 3) ÷ 2 = 4.

Since the reversed number is larger, the **original number** must be the smaller one, 47.

**∴ The correct answer is 47.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum of digits = 11 | (Reversed Number − Original Number) = 27.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/62c7862c7e652fe5d7a20c54ed5e28d5c847561439e5e26639b8d2fd6af2b650.png] 

Let the **tens digit** be x and the **units digit** be y.

⇒ Original Number = 10x + y

⇒ x + y = 11 --- (Eq. 1)

⇒ Reversed Number = 10y + x

⇒ (10y + x) − (10x + y) = 27

⇒ 9y − 9x = 27 ⇒ y − x = 3 --- (Eq. 2)

⇒ Adding (Eq. 1) and (Eq. 2): 2y = 14 ⇒ y = 7

⇒ Substituting y in (Eq. 1): x + 7 = 11 ⇒ x = 4

⇒ Original Number = 10(4) + 7 = 47

**∴ The correct answer is 47.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Difference between a number and its reverse

For a two-digit number, (10x + y) − (10y + x) = 9(x − y). This means the difference is always a multiple of 9.

Sum of a number and its reverse

For a two-digit number, (10x + y) + (10y + x) = 11(x + y). This means the sum is always a multiple of 11.

General Form

Any **two-digit number** with digits a and b can be expressed in expanded form as 10a + b.

questions.question: A cyclist travels from point A to B and back from B to A along the same route. On the onward journey, he covers one-third of the distance at 12 km/hr and the remaining distance at 18 km/hr. On the return journey, he covers half of the distance at 9 km/hr and the remaining distance at 18 km/hr. Find the average speed (in km/hr) for the entire round trip.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume total distance **AB = 108 km** (LCM of 3, 2, 9, 12, 18).

Onward time (A to B) = (36 km ÷ 12 km/hr) + (72 km ÷ 18 km/hr) = 3 + 4 = **7 hours**.

Return time (B to A) = (54 km ÷ 9 km/hr) + (54 km ÷ 18 km/hr) = 6 + 3 = **9 hours**.

Total distance = 108 + 108 = **216 km** | Total time = 7 + 9 = **16 hours**.

Average Speed = 216 ÷ 16 = **13.5 km/hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the one-way distance between **A** and **B** be **D**.

**Onward:** 1/3 D at 12 km/hr and 2/3 D at 18 km/hr.

**Return:** 1/2 D at 9 km/hr and 1/2 D at 18 km/hr.

**Formula:** **Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0cbeec2ddaa0c312634691ce0e23113fed42095283923e26d1fa7e71bc3c16f0.png] 

⇒ Total Distance = **2D**

⇒ Time for onward journey (T₁) = (D/3 ÷ 12) + (2D/3 ÷ 18) = D/36 + D/27 = (3D + 4D)/108 = **7D/108**

⇒ Time for return journey (T₂) = (D/2 ÷ 9) + (D/2 ÷ 18) = D/18 + D/36 = (2D + D)/36 = 3D/36 = **D/12**

⇒ Total Time = T₁ + T₂ = 7D/108 + D/12 = (7D + 9D)/108 = 16D/108 = **4D/27**

⇒ Average Speed = 2D ÷ (4D/27) = (2 × 27) ÷ 4 = 54 ÷ 4 = **13.5 km/hr**

**∴ The correct answer is 13.5 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a certain distance is covered at speed 'x' and the same distance is covered at speed 'y', then Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Equal Time

If a body travels at speed 'x' for time 't' and speed 'y' for the same time 't', then Average Speed = (x + y) ÷ 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers the following schemes on toys of the same marked price.

(A) Successive discounts of 5% and 21% on any number of toys bought.

(B) Successive discounts of 38%, 33% and 21% on any number of toys bought.

(C) 8% discount on the first 6 toys and 27% discount on each toy thereon.

(D) 3 toys free of cost on buying 7 toys.

A customer wants to buy 7 toys. Which of the above schemes is the least beneficial to her?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare the effective **discount percentages** for each scheme:

**Scheme A:** 5 + 21 − (5 × 21 ÷ 100) = 24.95%

**Scheme B:** Clearly much higher than 38% (first discount alone is 38%).

**Scheme C:** Average discount = [(6 × 8) + (1 × 27)] ÷ 7 = 75 ÷ 7 ≈ 10.71%

**Scheme D:** [Free items ÷ Total items] × 100 = 3 ÷ 10 × 100 = 30%

Comparing these, **Scheme C** offers the minimum discount.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Assume the **Marked Price (MP)** of each toy is **₹100**. For 7 toys, total **MP = ₹700**.

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Net Discount** = Total MP − Total SP

⇒ **Discount %** = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ae921229da36f8a23d6d72ddab5dfd64f29c565b7bdbb200e3ed6c79ad768ff.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Scheme A:** Net Discount % = 5 + 21 − (5 × 21)/100 = 24.95%.

⇒ **Scheme B:** This involves three successive discounts (38%, 33%, 21%). Even the first discount (38%) is greater than the others, making it highly beneficial.

⇒ **Scheme C:** Discount on first 6 toys = 6 × 8% of 100 = ₹48. Discount on 7th toy = 1 × 27% of 100 = ₹27. Total Discount = 48 + 27 = ₹75. Discount % = (75 ÷ 700) × 100 = 10.71%.

⇒ **Scheme D:** Buy 7 get 3 free implies 3 free out of 10 total toys. Discount % = (3 ÷ 10) × 100 = 30%.

⇒ Comparing all, 10.71% is the **lowest discount** value, making it the **least beneficial** to the customer.

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme C.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the equivalent single discount is given by [a + b − (ab ÷ 100)]%.

Buy X Get Y Free Discount

Marked Price and Selling Price

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × [ (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100 ]. The higher the discount, the lower the SP and the more beneficial it is for the buyer.

questions.question: The largest four-digit number which when divided by 14, 15 and 8 leaves remainder 4 in each case is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of the given divisors: 14, 15, and 8.

**LCM**(14, 15, 8) = 840.

The largest 4-digit multiple of 840 is 840 × 11 = 9240.

Add the required **remainder** (4) to this multiple: 9240 + 4 = 9244.

**∴ The correct answer is 9244.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 14, 15, 8

Remainder = 4

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = (Largest 4-digit multiple of **LCM**) + **Remainder**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3eea877a2886389c6451916792f42f1b38b46dcdf5b8dfe3d6e6b2882bfcb6e.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization: 14 = 2 × 7, 15 = 3 × 5, 8 = 2³.

⇒ **LCM** = 2³ × 3 × 5 × 7 = 8 × 3 × 5 × 7 = 840.

⇒ Largest 4-digit number = 9999.

⇒ Dividing 9999 by 840: 9999 ÷ 840 = 11 (Quotient) and 759 (Remainder).

⇒ Largest 4-digit multiple of 840 = 9999 − 759 = 9240.

⇒ Required number = 9240 + 4 = 9244.

**∴ The correct answer is 9244.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder

When a number N is divided by a, b, and c leaving the same remainder r, the general form is N = k × LCM(a, b, c) + r, where k is an integer.

Different Remainders

If N divided by a, b, c leaves remainders r₁, r₂, r₃ such that (a−r₁) = (b−r₂) = (c−r₃) = d, then N = k × LCM(a, b, c) − d.

LCM Calculation

LCM is the product of the highest powers of all prime factors involved in the given numbers.

questions.question: A wholesaler offers two options for a sofa set marked at ₹80,000: either a flat discount of 30% or two successive discounts of 20% and 12%. What is the difference in the selling price between the two options?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equivalent discount for successive discounts of 20% and 12% = 20 + 12 − (20 × 12 / 100) = 32 − 2.4 = 29.6%

Difference in discount percentage = 30% (Flat) − 29.6% (Successive) = 0.4%

Difference in **Selling Price** = 0.4% of **Marked Price**

Difference = 0.4% × 80,000 = 0.004 × 80,000 = 320

**∴ The correct answer is ₹320.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = ₹80,000

**Option 1**: Flat discount of 30%

**Option 2**: Successive discounts of 20% and 12%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D%) / 100

For successive discounts d₁ and d₂, Net SP = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21481dce205468f749ec4d789306b3cee0e3a58848b310c487c7cd230206fad2.png] 

⇒ **Selling Price 1 (Option 1)** = 80,000 × (70 / 100) = ₹56,000

⇒ Price after first discount in Option 2 = 80,000 × (80 / 100) = ₹64,000

⇒ **Selling Price 2 (Option 2)** = 64,000 × (88 / 100) = ₹56,320

⇒ **Difference in Selling Price** = ₹56,320 − ₹56,000 = ₹320

Thus, the difference between the two options is ₹320, which matches **Option (4)**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹320.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is (a + b − ab/100)%.

Marked Price and Selling Price

Selling Price is the price at which an item is sold after applying discounts on the **Marked Price (MP)**: SP = MP − Discount.

Comparison of Discounts

A single flat discount is usually greater than or equal to successive discounts of the same total numerical value (e.g., 30% is better for the customer than 20% + 10%).

questions.question: A school drum beats every 12 minutes, and the school bell rings every 18 minutes. If both sounded together at 9:00 AM, how many times will they sound together again before 11:00 AM?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The time interval for both to sound together is the **LCM** of their individual intervals.

**LCM(12, 18)** = **36 minutes**.

Total duration from **9:00 AM** to **11:00 AM** = 2 hours = **120 minutes**.

Number of times they sound again = **120 ÷ 36** = 3 (integer quotient).

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Frequency of **school drum** = every **12 min**

Frequency of **school bell** = every **18 min**

First simultaneous sound = **9:00 AM**

End time = **11:00 AM**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28c4754278f0d37a41b83e79003d915b4d81c1f89bbc4974d09fedafc441d28d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors of 12 = 2 × 2 × 3

⇒ Prime factors of 18 = 2 × 3 × 3

⇒ **LCM(12, 18)** = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = **36 minutes**

⇒ The instruments sound together at intervals of 36 minutes.

⇒ Time instances: 9:00 AM + 36 min = **9:36 AM**

⇒ 9:36 AM + 36 min = **10:12 AM**

⇒ 10:12 AM + 36 min = **10:48 AM**

⇒ 10:48 AM + 36 min = **11:24 AM** (which is after 11:00 AM)

⇒ The soundings occurring **again** before 11:00 AM are at 9:36, 10:12, and 10:48.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM for Simultaneous Events

To find when multiple cyclic events occur together, find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of their time periods.

Total Occurrences Formula

Total times = (Total Duration ÷ LCM) + 1, if the starting point is included. If only **again** is asked, exclude the start.

Time Conversion

Always convert time intervals to a common unit (usually minutes or seconds) before calculating the LCM.
